content: Sulfisoxazole is no longer available in the United States. If you are currently taking this medication, you should contact your doctor to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Sulfisoxazole is a sulfa-based antibiotic that works by eliminating bacteria responsible for infections, particularly those affecting the urinary tract and ears. It is important to note that antibiotics like sulfisoxazole are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. In some cases, sulfisoxazole may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Sulfisoxazole is available in tablet form and as a liquid suspension, both of which are taken orally. The usual dosing schedule involves taking the medication four times daily for a duration of 10 to 14 days or longer, depending on your doctor’s instructions. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of water. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is crucial to take sulfisoxazole exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less of the medication, and do not take it more frequently than directed. Before starting sulfisoxazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to sulfisoxazole, other sulfa drugs, diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), oral diabetes medications, or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially anticoagulants like warfarin (Coumadin), cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune), diabetes medications, methotrexate, phenytoin (Dilantin), and any vitamins or supplements. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease, asthma, severe allergies, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency, which is an inherited blood disorder. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking sulfisoxazole, contact your doctor immediately. Wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen when outdoors. Sulfisoxazole may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose of sulfisoxazole, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Sulfisoxazole may cause side effects. Mild side effects include diarrhea, dizziness or loss of balance, loss of appetite, and upset stomach. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include: Skin rash or other skin changes Sore throat Fever Headache Joint or muscle pain Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) Swelling of the lips or tongue Difficulty swallowing Fatigue Unusual bleeding or bruising Weakness If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store sulfisoxazole in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to sulfisoxazole. Do not share this medication with anyone else. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of sulfisoxazole, contact your doctor. Sulfisoxazole is marketed under the brand name Gantrisin® Pediatric Suspension. Combination products containing sulfisoxazole include Eryzole® and Pediazole®, both of which also contain erythromycin ethylsuccinate.
